title: Add log redaction + no-PII assertions for perf-canary request/telemetry path
author: Omar El-Sayed
description: Motivation: perf-canary must never emit or persist customer data. While the canary uses synthetic prompts, we still had a few sharp edges where (a) debug logging could print request bodies on errors and (b) some error/reporting paths would include raw prompt text / user-provided identifiers if they ever slipped through config. This PR adds explicit redaction + hard assertions so we fail-closed and keep logs/metrics safe. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce a centralized redaction helper for log fields and error payloads; (2) Add runtime assertions that enforce "synthetic-only" prompt sources (no external prompt injection), with an opt-out only for local dev; (3) Ensure we never log request bodies, prompt strings, or headers that may contain identifiers; (4) Add "safe fields" allowlist for alert webhook payloads so incident-bot never receives prompt content; (5) Add tests that simulate error paths (HTTP 4xx/5xx, timeouts, JSON decode errors) and verify log output + alert payload are redacted; (6) Add lightweight "no_pii" static checks on structured logging calls in canary request loop. Operational notes: if assertions trip in prod, the canary request will be dropped and counted under canary_safety_dropped_requests_total with reason=no_pii_guard; the process stays healthy and continues other model targets. Checklist: [x] No prompt strings in logs on success/error paths [x] No customer identifiers in metrics labels [x] Alert payload contains only model/region/version/baseline/observed deltas + links [x] Unit tests for redaction + guardrails [x] Docs note in README about dev-only override. Risk: low/medium; touches error handling and logging. Rollout: safe to deploy alongside existing canary; no config change required. Follow-ups: add a prometheus metric for redaction_invocations_total to track unexpected surfaces; consider moving dev-only override behind a build tag.

notable_snippet: Before: logger.Error("inference request failed", "err", err, "body", string(reqBody)) After: logger.Error("inference request failed", redaction.SafeFields(map[string]any{"err": err, "status": status, "model": model, "region": region})...) Note: request bodies and prompt content are never included; SafeFields drops/overwrites any key matching: prompt, input, messages, headers, authorization, cookie, user_id, org_id, customer_id.
